Read the full derivation, witnesses and counterexamplesCorrect option: 1 under the smallest-listed-upper-bound convention. The tight order is  Θ(lnnlnlnn). The original options use  O, so options 2 and 3 are valid looser upper bounds as well. Preserve that wording ambiguity when using this authentic question; the derivation identifies the tight order without treating three true upper bounds as logically exclusive.
Let  m=log2n. Ignoring rounding momentarily, taking a square root halves  m, so  S(m)=T(2m)  satisfies  S(m)=2S(m/2)+m. At depth  j, there are  2j  nodes, each with toll  m/2j. Total toll is exactly  m  per nonbase level. There are  Θ(logm)  levels, and the leaves contribute  O(m)  bounded base work. Hence  S(m)∈Θ(mlogm).
The floor does not invalidate this reasoning, but it requires control. Use a constant base region containing one and two. For  x≥4,  x/2≤⌊x⌋≤x. Taking base-two logarithms gives
m/2-1≤log2⌊x⌋≤m/2.
Repeated reduction bounds a level- j  logarithmic argument between  m/2j-2  and  m/2j. Therefore a level's toll is at most  m, and, while  2j≤m/4, at least  m-2j+1≥m/2. There are  Θ(logm)  significant levels and only  O(m)  leaves, giving matching upper and lower bounds despite rounding. Small endpoint levels alter constants only. Stopping solely below one would fail to terminate at one because its square root remains one.
Substitution returns  mlogm=Θ(lognloglogn). Option 2 adds a factor  n  to the tight upper bound. Option 3 replaces the leading  logn  by  n; its ratio to the tight bound is  n/logn→∞. Both are valid loose upper bounds. Option 4 omits the required  logn  factor and is too small. On  n=22h, all square roots are exact until the base, providing the independent check  S(2h)/2h=S(1)+h  under a unit base-two logarithmic toll.
